title: GHOSTroom shared definitions
description: Identifiers, timestamps, origins and evidence references shared by every GHOSTroom schema. Language-neutral: consumed by Swift and Python.

id.description: Opaque identifier. Compatible with the bridge's request_id rule and with uuid4 hex job/message ids.

blender_id.description: Bridge boot_id / scene_id (uuid4 hex, 32 lowercase hex).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp with a Z suffix, optional fractional seconds. Existing bridge epoch floats convert losslessly to millisecond precision.

text.description: Human-readable text. 16000 chars bounds a single message; the current relay limits chat text to 2000.

origin.description: Who produced an event or entry. Identifies the origin; it never owns the record.

id.description: Stable id within its kind, e.g. 'owner', 'codex', 'claude', 'bridge'.

provider.description: For agents: provider adapter name (codex, claude, gemini, openai, ...). Free string so no vendor is structurally essential.

lane.description: An agent's (or the user's) working lane. Lanes separate threads; they never hide information from the ledger.

stream_position.description: Delivery cursor contract. stream_id changes whenever the sequence restarts (for example a relay database reset), so a consumer holding a cursor for another stream_id must reset to 0 instead of skipping events.

job_evidence.description: Reference to a GhostBlender job. Evidence points at the job and its digests; it never copies the job's arguments or result payload.

state.description: Union of relay job states and device journal states.

device_digest.description: Device journal digest: sha256 of the delivered job JSON (agent/runtime/core.py:110).

relay_digest.description: Relay idempotency digest: sha256(operation, scene_id, canonical arguments) (agent/relay/store.py:116).

result_sha256.description: Optional hash of the stored result JSON, so evidence can be checked without being copied.

media_ref.description: Binary media by reference. Payload bytes never travel inside events or ledger entries.

uri.description: Where a consumer may fetch the bytes (relative relay path or app-local store key). Must not be a capability URL.
